summary: Round 2 re-review of all 16 units. The four round-1 fixes were each verified: the fins hook now correctly says thin insulation below the critical radius makes a small wire lose more heat and run cooler, consistent with the callout and q002; the Heisler warning is now correct (using 2L for L makes Fo four times too small for a given time and a time from a target Fo four times too long, and q002 is consistent); the finite-difference-transient step (c) now matches the numbers (surface limit 0.1279 s is just under the 1-D limit 0.1282 s, and the 2-D interior limit 0.064 s is the smallest); the condensation caption and both worked cases now state Nusselt theory is exact only for wave-free film to Re_delta of about 30 and conservative in the wavy-laminar range, with Re_delta = 223 and 268 labelled wavy-laminar and the 85 C case phrased as a surface held at 85 C. I then recomputed every numeric key and worked example independently in Python (conduction resistances and interface temperatures, fin q/eta/epsilon and critical radius including the 1.676 ratio and the 252 mm break-even radius, lumped capacitance, one-term roots zeta1 and C1 for every table row, semi-infinite erf and effusivity contact temperatures, finite-difference nodal values and all Gauss-Seidel iterates, explicit update and stability limits, flat-plate laminar, Hilpert, Dittus-Boelter and internal-flow energy balances, Rayleigh/Grashof and natural-convection correlations, Zuber including LN2 and lunar gravity, Nusselt condensation, LMTD, effectiveness-NTU and the LMTD cross-check, radiation networks and shields) and every key, tolerance and unit agrees with the stated data. Mechanisms, correlation constants, validity ranges and the n = 0.4 heating / 0.3 cooling exponents are correct. Scans of all eight packets found no tab or control characters inside LaTeX, no literal \uXXXX text, no [object Object] or undefined strings, no placeholder steps and no stale option-letter references in explanations. I found no real problems to report. This is an AI review only; the course still needs a subject-matter expert before engineering reliance.
